sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Tax Incidence vs. Tax Impact**: **Tax impact** refers to the initial point where the tax is legally imposed (statutory burden), whereas **tax incidence** refers to the ultimate economic burden of the tax after market adjustments and price shifts.
• **Progressive vs. Regressive Taxation**: **Progressive tax** takes a larger percentage of income as income rises (e.g., higher personal income tax slabs), reducing inequality; **regressive tax** takes a larger percentage from low-income earners (e.g., flat rate GST on essential items), widening inequality.
• **Proportional vs. Degressive Taxation**: **Proportional tax** levies a constant percentage regardless of income; **degressive tax** is progressive up to a certain point, after which it becomes proportional.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Tax-to-GDP Ratio** and **Tax Elasticity** measure revenue responsiveness and fiscal health.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Direct: Burden cannot be shifted (Income/Corporate Tax). Indirect: Burden shifted to consumers (GST, Customs Duty).

Avoidance: Using legal loopholes to minimize tax liability. Evasion: Illegal practice of deliberately not paying taxes.

Mains: Discussing Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) and domestic anti-avoidance measures.

Internalizing negative social costs into private market prices to align with social optimum.

items.definition: A provision under the Income Tax Act to ensure that companies reporting high book profits but paying zero tax due to exemptions pay a minimum specified percentage of book profit as tax.
A direct tax levied on specified digital services provided by non-resident e-commerce operators to Indian residents, aimed at taxing the digital economy where physical presence is absent.
A statutory framework empowering tax authorities to declare certain arrangements as 'impermissible avoidance arrangements' if designed primarily to obtain a tax benefit.
Income Tax Act 1961, CGST Act 2017, Finance Act (annual), and Parthasarathi Shome Committee on tax administration and GAAR.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **Special Economic Zones (SEZs) & Tax Havens**: SEZs located along coastal corridors (e.g., Kandla, SEEPZ) offer tax holidays to boost exports. Global tax havens (e.g., Mauritius, Cayman Islands) historically served as routing hubs for Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) into India.
• **Driving Advantages**: Concessional corporate tax rates, zero customs duty on capital goods imports, and relaxed regulatory compliances.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Complex litigation, retrospective taxation controversies, cascading effects in non-GST items (petroleum, real estate), and base erosion by multinational corporations.
• **Policy Interventions**: Faceless Assessment and Appeal schemes, Vivad se Vishwas scheme for dispute resolution, and India's commitment to the OECD/G20 Two-Pillar Solution for global minimum tax.

items.title: Mnemonic for Tax Incidence vs. Impact
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'Impact hits first, Incidence lands last.'
• **Decoded Meaning**: **Impact** is where the tax legally lands initially; **Incidence** is where the economic weight finally rests.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates confusion when UPSC swaps definitions in statements.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Direct Tax = Burden cannot be shifted (Income/Wealth); Indirect Tax = Burden shifts via price (GST/Excise).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that 'Indirect taxes are progressive because richer people consume more goods.' This is false; indirect taxes are inherently regressive because the tax rate is flat, consuming a larger proportion of a poor person's income than a rich person's income.

Mains Value Addition: Use terms like 'Fiscal Drag', 'Laffer Curve' (illustrating the relationship between tax rates and tax revenue), and 'Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS)' while writing answers on tax reforms and domestic resource mobilization.

keyTakeaways: Tax incidence depends on the price elasticity of demand and supply, not merely on who legally pays the tax.
Distinguishing between tax avoidance (legal exploitation of loopholes) and tax evasion (illegal concealment) is central to fiscal legislation like GAAR.
Modern tax administration in India is shifting towards digital transparency, faceless assessments, and alignment with global anti-base-erosion standards.
